rationale: Arsenal made Rogers their No.1 target with a £100m push (Times/Mirror/teamtalk June 21-23, Standard June 20); Chelsea prepared £90m bid, City and United also in race; Villa need a sale for financial rules.
No June 2026 deal reporting; Newcastle (12th, no Europe) want to keep their captain and are selling Gordon/Tonali instead; any exit would go to a big European side. Conditional question likely void.

Rodri has 12 months left and Real Madrid are his preferred destination, but as of June 12-22 reports Real Madrid are not expected to move this summer and Rodri will decide after the World Cup; likely stays.

Fiorentina did not activate the €10m option (TMW June 24) but are most likely to re-sign him on a discount loan-plus-option or lower fee; his agent prefers a Spurs stay, but he faces no route to minutes there.
Barcelona told Torres he will be sold and want ~€55m (final year of contract); Newcastle named the priority trackers (El Nacional/Chronicle May 8), with Villa and Spurs also linked.

Juventus sporting director Marco Ottolini is personally driving a move (~£26-28m) and has contacted Spurs (Gazzetta/Sportmediaset June 10, still active June 22); decision expected after the World Cup, with Cambiaso's exit the trigger.

Newcastle identified Watkins as a top striker target at ~£30m with AC Milan also interested (Sports Boom/GIVEMESPORT April 1); Villa have kept Watkins as core and his late-season form may deter a sale, so a 0.2 chance of staying is retained.

No credible June 2026 reporting of a Konsa deal; analysts call selling him 'a huge risk' (Birmingham Live June 7), he has 2 years left, and Villa are selling Rogers instead; Villa more likely moves to EPL money-club if it happens.
City told Savinho he can leave; talks with Spurs (~£50-60m) are progressing well per Romano and Standard (June 10), and Spurs want to move fast.

United have longstanding interest, already agreed personal terms last year and lead the race; Brighton resigned to selling at ~€80m and Baleba has his heart set on Old Trafford (TEAMtalk/FootballTransfers March-June).

City will listen to offers of ~€60-70m and Marmoush wants more minutes; Barcelona, Villa, Atletico, Milan and Spurs are the listed suitors, with Barcelona his preferred destination (SPORT/Flashscore). Conditional, and he may stay.
Al-Ittihad will not renew Fabinho's contract, which expires June 30, making him a free agent; Palmeiras, Flamengo, Cruzeiro and Fluminense are all chasing him and he will decide after the World Cup.
Arsenal opened talks and made Bouaddi a priority, with a ~€60-70m deal expected after the World Cup, though Lille rejected a €60m offer; PSG, Liverpool, Chelsea and Real Madrid also circle.
